clue.text: Simple angle on two levels

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it in the answer

parts.note: O-level and A-level were the two tiers of British school exams, giving O and A
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A plain, simple angle sitting across two levels, like geometry homework.
explanation.walkthrough: O-levels and A-levels were British school examinations, so 'two levels' gives O and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy, dim-witted person can be called simple, a near synonym for loutish stupidity.

clue.text: One tackled by a strong sort of player

indicators.note: one tackled by others is held among them, so it goes inside
sort of means a rearranged version of the letters

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone brought down by a powerful kind of player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' shuffles A STRONG to ORGANST, and 'tackled by' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays the church instrument with pipes is a kind of musical player.

clue.text: Struggle as a swimmer

explanation.surface: Someone struggling in the water as they swim.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to thrash about helplessly and also names a flatfish.

clue.text: Close to Honduras, little room for European

indicators.note: close to means the closing letter of the word

parts.note: lav is short for lavatory, the smallest room

explanation.surface: Near Honduras, there is scarcely room for a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like 'near', but means the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slav is a member of a group of peoples of eastern Europe.

clue.text: Stimulating piece behind box

indicators.note: one piece placed behind another comes after it in the answer

parts.note: to box is to spar
the king is a chess piece

explanation.surface: Something stimulating sits behind a box, as if a toy hidden in packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparking off an idea means provoking or stimulating it, so the participle fits.

clue.text: Papers surprisingly welcoming single currency at first, financial district showing discernment

indicators.note: welcoming means letting the others in, so they go inside
surprisingly means the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: single is one, Roman numeral I

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word

parts.note: the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: Financial papers welcoming a single currency, showing the City's shrewdness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' shuffles PAPERS to PERSPA, and 'welcoming' puts IC inside it. The City is London's financial centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen insight or shrewdness is discernment, a close synonym.

clue.text: Leader absent from serious party

indicators.note: the leading letter is missing from the word

parts.note: grave means serious

explanation.surface: A party leader has gone missing from serious politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader absent from' removes the G that starts GRAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A large lively dance event is a party, one with loud music.

clue.text: Something under one's foot lies on ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters are broken up and remade

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something under one's foot lies on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushioned inner sole of a shoe lies directly beneath the wearer's foot.

clue.text: Hot shooter, chap under discussion

indicators.note: something under discussion is spoken about, so a word said alike

parts.note: geezer is slang for a man, a chap

explanation.surface: A sharp-shooting man is being talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: GEEZER is British slang for a bloke.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot spring that shoots water into the air is a hot shooter.

clue.text: Girl about to throw up all over the place

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
to lob is to throw something up high

explanation.surface: A girl is about to be sick everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw up' reads as vomiting but means lob, tossing upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worldwide is found everywhere, so the phrase matches its sense of universal reach.

clue.text: Go without a piece of underwear in parody

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the attempt surrounds the rest

parts.note: a go is an attempt, a try
a vest is an undergarment in British usage

explanation.surface: Going without a piece of underwear in a parody performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside here. A vest in Britain is an undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotesque imitation or mockery of something serious is a parody, a close synonym.

clue.text: Model inserted, head down

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A model was put in place, head bowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' at the end looks part of 'head down', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means being dispirited, a sense of losing heart.

clue.text: Square, part of Tallinn in Estonia

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A town square forms part of Tallinn, Estonia's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is three times three, a square number.

clue.text: Cold, so brisk

explanation.surface: It is cold out, and so the walk is brisk.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both chilly weather and quick, agile movement, two distinct senses.

clue.text: Fruit far from 13, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving one that sounds alike

parts.note: 13 across means brisk, so its opposite is slow

explanation.surface: A fruit that is anything but quick, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 across is NIPPY, meaning quick; far from that is slow.
explanation.definitionFit: The blackthorn's small dark berry, used to flavour gin, is a fruit.

clue.text: Bob's delivery vehicle

definitions.meaning: to bob is to ... on water
a milk ... is a small electric delivery van in Britain

explanation.surface: Bob owns a delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: A milk float is a quiet electric cart once used for doorstep milk delivery in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to rest bobbing on water and also names a low delivery cart.

clue.text: A little shorter seems short

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something slightly shorter appears short.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse speech is brief and curt, a close synonym for being brusquely brief.

clue.text: Some tortoise with long hair, suffering trauma

parts.note: part of a tortoise is its shell
a shock is a thick mass of hair, so shocked means having one

explanation.surface: A long-haired tortoise in distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat stress or trauma was once called shell shock, so a traumatised person is described this way.

clue.text: Horse takes a breather around hot pile of waste

parts.note: a dun is a greyish-brown horse; takes just joins it to what follows

indicators.note: around means the breathing organ surrounds the next letter

parts.note: a fish breathes through its gill
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A horse pauses for breath near a steaming heap of waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A breather' sounds like a rest, but means a gill, the organ a fish breathes with.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap of manure is a pile of waste.

clue.text: Insurrection in small volume

parts.note: a volume is a book, an edition

explanation.surface: A rebellion recorded in a slim book.
explanation.definitionFit: Incitement to rebellion against the state is close in sense to insurrection.

clue.text: It's hot, as firm lip touches flap

indicators.note: touches means the flap sits right against the following pieces

parts.note: a tab is a small flap
CO is short for company, a firm
lip and sauce both mean cheek, impudence

explanation.surface: A firm lip pressing against a flap sounds like an oddly heated encounter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiery chilli condiment from Louisiana is the thing that is hot here.

clue.text: Error those in form overturned

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: a form is a school class, whose members are pupils

explanation.surface: An error by the class upset everything.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is a British school class.
explanation.definitionFit: A careless mistake is an error, a close synonym.

clue.text: Pound lapsing with penny off as a gesture

indicators.note: to pound is to beat, so the letters are battered into a new order
off means a letter is taken away

explanation.surface: The pound slipping, with the penny falling too, as a gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money but is the anagram signal: LAPSING without P is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A wave or nod is both a gesture and a signal sent to someone.

clue.text: Somewhere to retire with foreign money in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the rial is the currency of Iran and other states

explanation.surface: Someone retiring abroad, with foreign cash for their old age.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's den is where it withdraws to rest, so it is a place to retire to.

clue.text: One of fifty in the US, say

definitions.text: One of fifty in the US
definitions.meaning: the USA is made up of fifty ...

explanation.surface: Describing one of America's fifty, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a member of the American union and also means to declare.

clue.text: Fruit that's unattractive, grotesque, loathsome and ignoble, for starters

indicators.note: for starters points to the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A fruit described as ugly, grotesque, loathsome and ignoble.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jamaican citrus hybrid with a famously wrinkled skin is a fruit.

clue.text: Chorus of disapproval as alcohol mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, giving a word said the same way

parts.note: booze is slang for alcohol

explanation.surface: Jeers break out when drink is brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeers shouted by a crowd form a chorus of disapproval.

clue.text: One side remaining

explanation.surface: Only one side remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the side opposite right and also means still remaining.

clue.text: Locate flag, then aim

indicators.note: then puts the second piece after the first

parts.note: on a golf course the flag marking the hole is the pin
to aim is to point

explanation.surface: Instructions for marking a target: locate the flag, then aim.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something exactly is to locate it precisely, a close synonym.

clue.text: Gate only opening and closing? Little sign

indicators.note: only the opening and closing letters are kept, the first and last of the word

parts.note: mini means little

explanation.surface: A gate that does nothing but open and close, with a small sign on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twins are one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Royal attendant's sound barrier

indicators.note: sound signals that the phrase is spoken, giving a word said the same way

parts.note: a royal residence is a palace; an attendant is an aide; the 's stands for is and is no letter

explanation.surface: The noise made by a royal servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palace aide' run together gives the word entered.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence of pointed stakes is a defensive barrier.

clue.text: Hot bread, one left out

indicators.note: out means one letter is dropped from the bread

parts.note: stollen is a German fruit bread

explanation.surface: Warm bread fresh from the oven, with one left over.
explanation.walkthrough: Stollen has two Ls; 'one left out' removes just one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for stolen goods is hot, as in a hot car.
